front: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
back: Sound is passed on by vibrating particles; a vacuum has no particles (no medium).
Compression: particles closer together (higher pressure). Rarefaction: particles further apart (lower pressure).

front: Speed of sound in solids, liquids and gases?
back: Generally fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases.

front: What is the **quality** (timbre) of a sound?
back: What makes the same note sound different on different instruments; it depends on the waveform shape.

front: How do you measure the speed of sound in air?
back: Measure a large distance; time from seeing a sound made to hearing it; repeat, average; speed = distance ÷ time.
